articles.title: DRC Ebola Cases Exceed 2,000 Amid Health Worker Strikes
articles.excerpt: Strikes disrupt critical response efforts as the outbreak escalates in the Democratic Republic of Congo.
articles.image_caption: Health workers in protective equipment during an Ebola response operation (Wikimedia Commons)
articles.nri_angle: The ongoing Ebola outbreak and health worker strikes in the DRC could impact travel and health security for the Indian diaspora with connections to the region.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: A Daily Cup of Dahi and a 30-Minute Walk May Slow Aging at the Cellular Level, Study Finds
articles.excerpt: A clinical trial published in Aging showed that yogurt, moderate exercise, and dietary tweaks reduced the pace of biological aging by 2.2% in just 12 weeks — independent of weight loss.
articles.image_caption: A bowl of yogurt — consuming 100 grams daily was part of the anti-aging intervention studied by researchers (Wikimedia Commons)
articles.nri_angle: Dahi (plain yogurt) has been a daily staple in Indian households for generations — this clinical trial validates that the tradition may carry real anti-aging benefits at the cellular level.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: Structured Lifestyle Changes Improved Brain Health by 55% in At-Risk Adults, Landmark AAIC Study Shows
articles.excerpt: The LatAm-FINGERS trial, presented at the Alzheimer's Association International Conference 2026 in London and published in The Lancet, found that coached exercise, adapted diets, cognitive training, and social engagement dramatically boosted memory and thinking in older adults across 11 countries.
articles.image_caption: An fMRI brain scan — a landmark AAIC study found structured lifestyle changes improved cognitive function by 55% in at-risk adults (Wikimedia Commons)
articles.nri_angle: South Asians face elevated dementia risk factors by midlife. This landmark trial shows that the coached lifestyle changes most effective for brain health — group exercise, adapted diets, social engagement — mirror traditions already embedded in diaspora communities.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: One in Three Asian Americans With Serious Distress Goes Untreated, Largest NYC Study Finds
articles.excerpt: A population-based study of 6,648 Asian American adults in New York City found that stigma, cost, and a lack of culturally matched therapists are leaving a fast-growing community without the mental health care it needs.
articles.image_caption: Insight Therapy Solutions
articles.nri_angle: The cultural barriers to mental health care identified in this NYC study — stigma, self-reliance, lack of matched therapists — are replicated across South Asian communities in the US, Canada, and UK, compounding the diaspora's already elevated cardiovascular risk.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: An Anti-Inflammatory Diet Cut Dementia Risk by 29% — and Your Dadi's Kitchen Had It Right All Along
articles.excerpt: A landmark 15-year study in JAMA Network Open found that diets rich in vegetables, legumes, and whole grains — staples of traditional South Asian cooking — significantly lower the odds of cognitive decline, even in people already showing early signs of Alzheimer's.
articles.image_caption: Fresh vegetables, legumes, and whole grains — staples of anti-inflammatory eating patterns linked to lower dementia risk
articles.nri_angle: Traditional South Asian diets rich in anti-inflammatory ingredients like turmeric, dal, and whole grains align closely with the eating pattern shown to cut dementia risk — a critical finding for a community at elevated cardiometabolic risk.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: Five Weeks of Walking With Poles Cut Depression Symptoms in Half, a Landmark Trial Found
articles.excerpt: A randomized controlled trial published in the Journal of Affective Disorders found that supervised Nordic walking led to clinical remission in up to 53% of participants — offering a low-cost, stigma-free path to mental health care that could resonate in South Asian communities.
articles.image_caption: Nordic walking engages up to 90 percent of the body's muscles, turning a simple walk into a full-body workout
articles.nri_angle: Community walking groups are already a fixture in South Asian diaspora neighborhoods — this study suggests adding structure to what people already do could yield clinical-grade mental health benefits in a culturally comfortable, stigma-free way.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: 14 Indian Cities Rank Among the World's Most Heat-Vulnerable. Here's What That Means for Your Family Back Home.
articles.excerpt: A new Oxford University analysis of cities at greatest risk from extreme heat placed Nagpur, Chennai, Bengaluru, and 11 other Indian cities in the global top 50 — driven not just by soaring temperatures but by limited infrastructure, aging populations, and socioeconomic vulnerability.
articles.image_caption: Indian cities face compounding heat risks from soaring temperatures and limited cooling infrastructure
articles.nri_angle: NRIs with aging parents in any of 14 Indian cities ranked among the world's most heat-vulnerable need a concrete plan — from cooling infrastructure to medication reviews — before the next summer peak.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: South Asians Face Higher Heart Risk by 45 Despite Healthier Habits, Major Study Finds
articles.excerpt: A decade-long Northwestern study of 2,700 adults reveals a troubling paradox: South Asians report better diets and lower alcohol use but develop prediabetes and hypertension at double the rate of white Americans by midlife.
articles.image_caption: A blood pressure screening — a major new study finds South Asians face significantly higher cardiovascular risk by age 45 (Wikimedia Commons)
articles.nri_angle: South Asian Americans face uniquely elevated cardiovascular risk that standard BMI and lifestyle metrics fail to capture, demanding earlier screening and culturally tailored health interventions.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: From Bhag Club to Bombay On Foot: How India's Run Club Boom Is Rewriting the Wellness Playbook
articles.excerpt: Across India's cities, running clubs are replacing bar crawls as the new social ritual — and the movement is resonating with the diaspora seeking community beyond the treadmill.
articles.image_caption: Runners gather for an early morning group run in an Indian city park
articles.nri_angle: NRIs watching India's community fitness explosion are finding parallels in their own cities — and many are launching or joining similar run clubs abroad, bridging diaspora loneliness with the Indian ethos of collective wellness.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: The Science Is Settling: What 104 Clinical Trials Say About Turmeric's Real Health Benefits
articles.excerpt: A sweeping meta-analysis of over 100 randomized controlled trials finds that curcumin supplementation significantly lowers blood sugar, cholesterol, and inflammation — but the dose and form matter more than your grandmother's golden milk recipe.
articles.image_caption: Fresh turmeric root and ground curcumin powder, staples of South Asian kitchens
articles.nri_angle: For South Asians who grew up with turmeric as kitchen medicine, the largest-ever clinical review validates what their grandmothers always said — while revealing that traditional culinary doses and modern supplements are not the same thing.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: India's Workers Are Losing 22 Days a Year to Extreme Heat. The Health Toll Is Even Worse.
articles.excerpt: A new report projects that rising temperatures will cost India 5.8 percent of its working hours annually, while heatstroke deaths mount and the monsoon brings no relief — forcing a rethink of how the country protects its most vulnerable.
articles.image_caption: A construction worker in Kolkata — new research warns Indian workers will lose an average of 22.5 days annually to extreme heat (Wikimedia Commons)
articles.nri_angle: NRIs whose families work in heat-exposed sectors face mounting health risks, and diaspora members visiting India during summer increasingly encounter dangerous conditions they are no longer acclimatised to.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: India's Food Safety Regulator Just Called Out Dozens of 'Healthy' Brands. Here's Why NRIs Should Care.
articles.excerpt: From Lotte's bread to Ferrero's Kinder Joy to Emami's cooking oil, FSSAI's unprecedented crackdown on misleading labels is exposing how some of India's most familiar packaged foods are not what they claim to be.
articles.image_caption: The Food Safety and Standards Authority of India (FSSAI) has issued notices to dozens of brands for misleading health claims (Wikimedia Commons)
articles.nri_angle: Many flagged brands — Emami, Lotte, Ferrero — are staples of NRI grocery shopping worldwide, and misleading 'healthy' labels on Indian packaged food directly affect diaspora consumers making dietary decisions.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: By 40, Half of South Asian Women in the UK May Develop a Chronic Disease, Landmark Study Warns
articles.excerpt: A Queen Mary University study of 23,000 British Bangladeshi and Pakistani participants reveals that mental health and cardiovascular conditions cluster early — and the order they arrive in matters.
articles.image_caption: The study, published in The Lancet, warns that half of South Asian women in the UK may develop a chronic disease by age 40 (Wikimedia Commons)
articles.nri_angle: South Asian diaspora communities in the UK, US, and Canada face elevated cardiovascular and mental health risks that begin a decade earlier than standard screening catches — this study argues for culturally tailored early intervention.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: Nita Ambani Receives Key to Tampa and Humanitarian Award as Indian-American Doctors Launch Cross-Border Health Alliance
articles.excerpt: The AAPI convention drew over 2,000 physicians and unveiled targeted heart screenings for South Asians alongside a new India-America healthcare partnership
articles.image_caption: Nita Ambani, Chairperson of Reliance Foundation (Wikimedia Commons)
articles.nri_angle: Indian-American physicians make up 10% of all US doctors; new AAPI heart screening initiative directly targets South Asian cardiovascular risks that affect every NRI family
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: Ayurveda Has Become a $20 Billion Global Industry. The Diaspora Is Still Figuring Out How to Feel About It.
articles.excerpt: From ashwagandha gummies at Whole Foods to AI-powered dosha apps, India's ancient wellness traditions are everywhere — raising questions about appropriation, identity, and who profits
articles.image_caption: Traditional Ayurvedic herbs and preparations that have found their way into mainstream Western wellness
articles.nri_angle: NRIs watch their grandmothers' home remedies repackaged as premium Western wellness products — the $20B Ayurveda market raises urgent questions about cultural identity and who profits from Indian traditions
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: Your Smartwatch Wasn't Built for You: Why South Asians Need to Rethink Wearable Health Data
articles.excerpt: Wearable health devices are a $131 billion market, but their algorithms were trained on Western bodies — here is what diaspora Indians should actually track and why
articles.image_caption: moonhouse via flickr (BY)
articles.nri_angle: South Asians face up to 4x higher cardiovascular risk yet wearable health algorithms are calibrated for Western populations — every NRI with a smartwatch needs to know what the numbers actually mean for them

articles.title: India's Generic Ozempic Revolution Hits a Wall as Dr. Reddy's Halts Semaglutide Production
articles.excerpt: The supply disruption could delay affordable access to semaglutide for millions in India and Canada until late October — a setback for NRIs who had been counting on cheaper alternatives to manage diabetes and weight.
articles.image_caption: Semaglutide injection pens used for diabetes and weight management treatment
articles.nri_angle: NRIs in India and Canada who rely on affordable generic semaglutide face supply gaps until late October, forcing mid-treatment brand switches.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: Your Monsoon Survival Kit: What Every NRI Needs to Know Before Landing in India This Summer
articles.excerpt: From dengue prevention to water safety and gut health, a practical guide for diaspora travellers navigating India's rainy season — when familiar cities become unfamiliar health minefields.
articles.image_caption: India's monsoon season brings relief from summer heat but also heightened health risks for returning NRI travellers
articles.nri_angle: NRIs visiting India during monsoon face amplified health risks as their immune systems have adapted to Western conditions — this guide covers prevention from dengue to gut health.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: Aging Far From Home: How Indian-American Seniors Are Building Support Systems That Don't Exist in Mainstream America
articles.excerpt: From community-run senior centres in Queens to Ayurvedic wellness retreats in California, diaspora Indians are pioneering culturally rooted approaches to aging — because the Western eldercare model was never built for them.
articles.image_caption: The Indian-American community in neighborhoods like Jackson Heights, Queens builds support networks for aging diaspora members
articles.nri_angle: Indian-American seniors face a culturally unique eldercare gap — organisations like India Home and SASA are building the support systems mainstream America never designed for them.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: A Single 'Polypill' Cut Heart Failure Hospitalizations by 60 Percent in a Landmark Trial — and It Could Reshape How Millions Manage the Disease
articles.excerpt: The POLY-HF trial, led by Indian-American cardiologist Dr. Ambarish Pandey, found that combining three heart failure drugs into one daily pill dramatically improved adherence and survival — a breakthrough with outsized implications for South Asians, who face the world's highest burden of cardiovascular disease.
articles.image_caption: AIIMS New Delhi — a landmark polypill trial has shown that combining four heart failure drugs into one tablet cut hospitalizations by 60 percent
articles.nri_angle: South Asians bear 60% of the world's heart disease burden and face higher cardiovascular risk by age 45 — a simplified polypill strategy could transform medication compliance for diaspora families managing chronic conditions across borders.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: Half of All Americans Now Feel Lonely at Least Once a Week — and the Diaspora Is Not Immune
articles.excerpt: A surge in isolation is driving real health consequences, from depression to heart disease. For NRIs who left dense social networks behind, the crisis cuts deeper.
articles.image_caption: A solitary figure, reflecting the growing isolation crisis
articles.nri_angle: Indian immigrants face elevated loneliness risks after leaving dense family and community networks; older NRIs joining children abroad are especially vulnerable.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: Extreme Humid Heat Cuts Brain Blood Flow by a Third and Forces the Heart Into Overdrive — Here's What That Means for You
articles.excerpt: A scientific simulation reveals how quickly high humidity overwhelms the body's defences, with particular risks for South Asians carrying undiagnosed hypertension and prediabetes
articles.image_caption: Extreme heat conditions — new research shows humid heat can cut brain blood flow by a third and force the heart into overdrive (Wikimedia Commons)
articles.nri_angle: South Asian Americans face elevated hypertension and prediabetes risk by their mid-40s, making them especially vulnerable to the cardiovascular and neurological toll of humid heat waves sweeping U.S. cities with large NRI populations.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: An Anti-Inflammatory Diet Can Cut Dementia Risk by Nearly a Third — Even After Alzheimer's Has Begun in Your Brain
articles.excerpt: A 15-year study of nearly 1,900 older adults found that eating foods rich in antioxidants and healthy fats lowered dementia rates by up to 29 percent, even in people whose blood already carried elevated Alzheimer's biomarkers — and the traditional Indian pantry is a natural fit.
articles.image_caption: Colourful fruits, vegetables, and spices — staples of an anti-inflammatory diet linked to lower dementia risk
articles.nri_angle: Traditional Indian diets rich in turmeric, lentils, and spices are naturally anti-inflammatory — but NRIs who shift to processed Western foods may be losing a dietary advantage that could protect against Alzheimer's.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: Five Extra Minutes of Sleep and Two Minutes of Exercise a Day Could Add a Full Year to Your Life
articles.excerpt: A landmark UK Biobank study of nearly 60,000 adults finds that tiny, simultaneous improvements in sleep, physical activity, and diet compound into as much as 9.4 extra years of disease-free living — and the findings carry outsized implications for South Asians.
articles.image_caption: Fresh vegetables, whole grains, and fruits — small dietary improvements that compound over time
articles.nri_angle: South Asians face elevated cardiometabolic risk at lower BMI thresholds — this study shows that even tiny concurrent lifestyle changes can yield outsized health gains for diaspora professionals struggling to make time for wellness.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: A Single Blood Test Can Now Screen for 10 Cancers — and Zydus and Apollo Are Bringing It to India
articles.excerpt: The FDA-designated multi-cancer detection test, built by Guardant Health, uses a simple blood draw to catch bladder, breast, colorectal and seven other cancers before symptoms appear
articles.image_caption: A laboratory technician examines blood sample vials for diagnostic testing
articles.nri_angle: NRIs who schedule health check-ups during visits to India could access a validated multi-cancer blood test through Apollo's nationwide network, and South Asians face distinctive cancer risks that make early multi-cancer screening especially relevant.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk
